definitions: To become involved in a negative or difficult situation, often against one's will.
To be pulled into a lower or worse state, often emotionally or morally.
To be negatively influenced by others or by circumstances.
examples: She didn't want to get dragged down into their argument.
His grades started to get dragged down by his new friends.
It's easy to get dragged down by constant bad news.
Don't let their negativity get you dragged down.
pastTenses: got dragged down, gotten dragged down
